Miami-Dade has multiple correctional facilities operated by MDC Corrections.

Finding information about an inmate in Miami-Dade County is straightforward when you know where to look. The Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation Department maintains searchable records for all individuals currently in custody at county facilities. Whether you're searching for a family member, friend, or need to verify someone's detention status, this guide provides official resources and step-by-step instructions for the Miami-Dade County Florida inmate lookup process.

How to Search Miami-Dade County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official Miami-Dade County inmate search portal at the Corrections and Rehabilitation website. This is the fastest and most reliable method to locate current inmates.
  2. Enter the inmate's full name or booking number in the search field. If you have a booking number, using it will return results more quickly than a name search.
  3. Review the search results, which display the inmate's location, charges, bail information, and custody status. Information updates throughout the day as bookings occur.
  4. For historical records or inmates no longer in the system, contact the Miami-Dade County Corrections office directly by phone or visit in person during business hours.
  5. If the person is not found in the county jail system, check the Florida Department of Corrections inmate locator to see if they have been transferred to state custody or are serving a sentence in the state prison system.

Bail Bond Information for Miami-Dade County

In Miami-Dade County, bail is typically set during the first appearance or arraignment hearing, which usually occurs within 24 hours of arrest. If a defendant cannot afford to post bail in full, they may use the services of a bail bondsman. A licensed bondsman will charge a non-refundable fee, typically 10 percent of the total bail amount, to secure the defendant's release. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, a bondsman's fee would be $1,000. This fee is paid directly to the bondsman and is not returned, even if the charges are later dismissed.

Bail bondsmen in Miami-Dade County are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Many operate near the county jail facilities and courthouse for convenience. Defendants who fail to appear for their scheduled court date will forfeit their bail and face additional criminal charges. If you need to arrange bail for an inmate, contact a local bail bond agent as soon as possible after booking. The Miami-Dade County Corrections website and court system can provide referrals to licensed bondsmen serving the area.

Visitation Rules at Miami-Dade County Jail

  • Inmate Identification: Know the inmate's full name and booking number before visiting. This information is available through the official inmate search.
  • Visitation Hours: General visitation is typically available on weekdays and weekends during scheduled hours. Contact the facility directly to confirm current hours, as they may change seasonally or due to security procedures.
  • Dress Code: Visitors must dress appropriately—no revealing clothing, gang-affiliated colors, or offensive graphics. Clothing must cover shoulders, torso, and extend to the knees.
  • Video Visitation: Miami-Dade County Jail offers video visitation options for those unable to visit in person. This service is available through the facility's approved vendor, often with a small fee per session.
  • Children and Minors: Children under 18 may visit but must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times. Some facilities have restrictions on the number of children permitted per visit.

What to Expect After Arrest in Miami-Dade County

  1. Booking: Upon arrival at a detention facility, the arrestee is photographed, fingerprinted, and questioned about personal information, medical history, and gang affiliations. Belongings are inventoried and stored.
  2. Medical Screening: A nurse or medical professional conducts a health assessment to identify any medical conditions, medications needed, or communicable diseases. This information protects both the inmate and facility staff.
  3. Classification: Based on the charges, criminal history, and behavior, the inmate is assigned a custody level (minimum, medium, or maximum) and placed in an appropriate housing unit.
  4. First Appearance/Arraignment: Within 24 hours of arrest, the inmate appears before a judge. The judge notifies them of their charges, rights, and bail status. This is the earliest opportunity to request a bail reduction or release on recognizance.
  5. Transfer: If convicted and sentenced to state prison, the inmate is transferred to the Florida Department of Corrections reception facility for processing into the state system.

How to Contact Miami-Dade County Jail

Direct contact with Miami-Dade County Corrections staff can help clarify visitation rules, confirm release dates, or report concerns about an inmate's safety or care. Phone lines are typically available during business hours, though you may also submit inquiries online or visit a facility in person. Have the inmate's booking number or full name ready when you call for the fastest service.

Frequently Asked Questions — Miami-Dade County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Miami-Dade County jail?

Use the official Miami-Dade County inmate search portal at the Corrections and Rehabilitation website. Enter the person's full name or booking number. Results show current location, charges, bail amount, and custody status. Updates occur throughout the day as new bookings are processed.

How long does booking take in Miami-Dade County?

The booking process typically takes 2–4 hours, depending on how busy the facility is and the complexity of the case. During this time, the arrestee is photographed, fingerprinted, and medically screened. After booking is complete, they may be moved to a housing unit and appear before a judge within 24 hours.

Can I visit an inmate at Miami-Dade County jail?

Yes, visitation is permitted during scheduled hours. Visitors must dress appropriately, present identification, and know the inmate's full name and booking number. Video visitation is also available for those unable to visit in person. Contact the facility for specific visitation schedules and any temporary restrictions.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If an inmate is not found in the Miami-Dade County system, they may have been transferred to the Florida Department of Corrections state prison system, released on bail or recognizance, or booked in a different county. Check the state DOC inmate locator and nearby county facilities. Court records can also clarify disposition of the case.

How do I send money to an inmate in Miami-Dade County?

Miami-Dade County inmates can receive commissary funds through approved vendors. The Corrections department website lists accepted payment methods, including online transfers, mail, and phone deposits. Funds are added to the inmate's account within 24 hours and can be used for canteen items, phone calls, and hygiene products. Processing fees may apply depending on the payment method chosen.
